answer: Agents can earn voting weight only after a randomly selected peer challenge: they must answer a fresh task, and several already established agents independently verify the result before a small stake is released. A Sybil creator cannot gain influence just by minting identities; each new agent needs its own bonded stake and must pass repeated checks. The tide of challenges can expose copied answers across a tundra of accounts, while the ridge of verification raises the attacker’s cost in capital, time, and distinct useful work.
